一.meaning: A single, unbroken line stretches across the flat Ground (地), representing the simplest, fundamental unit of all things.
一.onyomi: Itch — I have an itch on my arm, just one tiny spot.
一.kunyomi: Hit — You hit the bullseye with just one perfect shot.

二.meaning: Two (二) parallel lines, clearly distinct, yet side-by-side, always in pairs.
二.onyomi: Knee — My knees started to ache after walking two miles.
二.kunyomi: Foot — I have two feet, one for each shoe.

九.meaning: The Nine (九) radical itself, a single stroke that curls and hooks, almost completing a circle but falling just short.
九.onyomi: Kyu is always late, arriving nine minutes after class starts.
九.kunyomi: Coconuts — I'm trying to juggle nine coconuts, but they keep falling.

七.meaning: The Seven (七) radical, a sharp angle and a long stroke, like a scythe cutting through the air.
七.onyomi: Sheila counts exactly seven sheep returning to the barn each evening.
七.kunyomi: Nana — My Nana loves to tell me seven different stories before bed.

人.meaning: A Person (人) stands with two legs firmly planted, ready to move or observe the world.
人.onyomi: Gin — A gin bottle stood alone, waiting for a person to pour a drink.
人.kunyomi: Hit — A person can get hit by a stray ball if they're not careful.

入.meaning: The Enter (入) radical looks like two legs stepping through a doorway, moving from outside to within.
入.onyomi: New — We're about to enter a new phase of our lives.
入.kunyomi: Eve — Eve steps cautiously, ready to enter the forbidden garden.

八.meaning: Two delicate Fins spread wide, perfectly balanced, allowing a creature to glide through the water.
八.onyomi: Hatch — Eight tiny chicks hatch from their eggs, one after another.
八.kunyomi: Yacht — We saw eight magnificent yachts sailing across the bay.

十.meaning: A perfect Cross (十) stands tall, symbolizing completion, the end of a count.
十.onyomi: Joe measures out exactly ten feet of cable for the lock he's fixing.
十.kunyomi: Toe — I counted ten toes on my feet, all wiggling.

三.meaning: The solid Ground (地) supports not just one, but two (二) additional layers, creating a distinct stack.
三.onyomi: Sand — Three grains of sand fell through my fingers.
三.kunyomi: Me — There are three of me in this mirror, a trick of the light.

上.meaning: A tiny Toe is delicately balanced directly above the Ground (地), implying something positioned higher.
上.onyomi: Joe carefully places the last piece of the lock above the doorframe.
上.kunyomi: Way — This is the way up, above the clouds.

下.meaning: A curious Toe peeks out from just Below the surface of the Ground (地), barely visible.
下.onyomi: Carlos quickly ducks down, hiding below the counter from his customers.
下.kunyomi: Sheila looks below the sheep for her lost lamb, getting her hands dirty.

大.meaning: A Big (大) person stands with arms and legs spread wide, taking up a truly immense space.
大.onyomi: Tai, the massive rugby player, is known for his large presence on the field.
大.kunyomi: Oh, my! What a large elephant!

女.meaning: A graceful Woman (女) kneels, perhaps in prayer or tending to a child, her posture soft and gentle.
女.onyomi: Joe politely asks the woman if she needs help with her heavy bags.
女.kunyomi: On a woman's lap, a child sleeps peacefully.

山.meaning: Three towering peaks of a Mountain (山) pierce the sky, rugged and majestic.
山.onyomi: Senna expertly navigates her race car up the winding roads of the mountain.
山.kunyomi: Yawn! Climbing a mountain always makes me tired.

川.meaning: The gentle currents of a River (川) flow continuously, carving its path through the land.
川.onyomi: Senna drives her race car alongside a fast-flowing stream, enjoying the view.
川.kunyomi: A thirsty cow drinks from the cool stream.

土.meaning: A simple mound of rich, dark Dirt, ready for planting, holds the promise of life.
土.onyomi: Tova digs her hands deep into the fertile soil of her garden, preparing for spring.
土.kunyomi: He dropped his precious sushi right in the dirt!

千.meaning: A single stroke crosses another, representing a vast, immeasurable number, like a Thousand (千) grains of sand.
千.onyomi: Senna speeds past a sign indicating a thousand kilometers to the finish line.
千.kunyomi: Cheese! A thousand pieces of cheese piled high!

子.meaning: A small, adorable Child (子) with outstretched arms looks up with wide, curious eyes.
子.onyomi: Sheila gently teaches the child how to feed the baby lambs on her farm.
子.kunyomi: Cora, the nosy neighbor, always watches the children play in the park.

小.meaning: Three tiny dots scattered across a surface, symbolizing something incredibly Small (小) and delicate.
小.onyomi: Sho, the surfer, found a little seashell on the beach, perfectly formed.
小.kunyomi: The little baby had rosy cheeks and a tiny smile.

中.meaning: A bold line pierces straight through the Middle (中) of a square, going directly into its core.
中.onyomi: Cho quickly puts all the aromatic spices in the pot, right in the middle of the simmering broth.
中.kunyomi: He has a knack for finding things hidden in the middle of a messy room.

五.meaning: The "Five (五)" radical, with its two horizontal lines sandwiching a cross, looks like a tally counter that has just completed its fifth stroke, signaling the end of a group of five.
五.onyomi: Cora counts the five cookies she's allowed to eat today, making sure she doesn't go over.
五.kunyomi: It's always a challenge to count to five on your fingers with mittens on.

六.meaning: A heavy "Lid" is precariously balanced on top of a cluster of "Fins", making it look like a strange creature with exactly six appendages struggling to stay upright.
六.onyomi: A giant "rock" sits perfectly balanced on six small pebbles, defying gravity.
六.kunyomi: The cow let out a long, drawn-out "moo" exactly six times before finally settling down.

円.meaning: A perfectly round "Lid" is placed on top of a giant, spherical "Head (首)", emphasizing the flawless circular shape of both.
円.onyomi: At the "end" of the race, the runners completed a full circle around the track.
円.kunyomi: He used a "marker" to draw a perfect circle on the whiteboard.

天.meaning: The "Heaven (天)" radical shows a vast, overarching line above, like the endless sky, with a smaller figure below reaching up, trying to touch the immense expanse of the heavens.
天.onyomi: Counting to "ten" while looking up at the vast heavens, he felt incredibly small.
天.kunyomi: A mat's surface felt like soft clouds when she lay down and looked up at the heavens.

日.meaning: The "Sun (日)" radical, a perfect rectangle with a single horizontal line, depicts the sun at its zenith, marking the brightest part of a day.
日.onyomi: Every "niche" in the ancient wall fills with sunlight at a different time of day.
日.kunyomi: Hina wakes up early every day to bake fresh bread, greeting the rising sun.

月.meaning: The "Moon (月)" radical, with its distinct curved shape and internal lines, perfectly captures the changing phases of the moon that define a month.
月.onyomi: You "get" to see the full moon only once a month, if the clouds permit.
月.kunyomi: Sushi is best eaten under the full moon once a month, a special occasion.

木.meaning: The "Tree (木)" radical vividly illustrates a sturdy trunk with spreading branches and deep roots, the quintessential image of a majestic tree.
木.onyomi: He read a "book" about the ancient forests and the many types of trees within them.
木.kunyomi: Kiki laughs as she scrambles to the top of a tall tree, enjoying the view.

水.meaning: The "Water (水)" radical cleverly depicts a central stream with two smaller splashes on either side, perfectly capturing the dynamic flow of water.
水.onyomi: He wore a diving "suit" to explore the mysterious depths of the water.
水.kunyomi: Don't "mis"interpret the calm surface; there's a strong current under the water.

火.meaning: The "Fire (火)" radical vividly shows a central blaze with two smaller embers flickering upwards, embodying the dynamic and destructive nature of fire.
火.onyomi: Carlos quickly cooks his tacos over a fierce fire, the flames licking at the pan.
火.kunyomi: Hina uses a small fire to bake her bread, carefully controlling the heat.

出.meaning: Two identical "Mountain (山)" radicals are stacked, with a deliberate gap in the middle, as if something has just pushed its way out from between the peaks, creating an exit.
出.onyomi: “Shoot” out of here, make a quick exit before anyone sees you!
出.kunyomi: At the end of the "day", everyone wants to exit the building and go home.

右.meaning: A Narwhal uses its long, pointed tusk to push a stubborn Mouth (口) over to the correct side.
右.onyomi: Yusuf always draws his brooding figures pointing to the right, never the left.
右.kunyomi: Migi — 'me gee' — you'll give me a gee-whiz reaction if you can point to the right spot.

四.meaning: Imagine a tiny, square Mouth (口) that suddenly sprouts four wobbly Legs, trying to scuttle away.
四.onyomi: Sheila counts her sheep, always making sure she has exactly four in a pen.
四.kunyomi: Yo! Count to four with me: Yo, ro, shi, ku!

左.meaning: A Narwhal keeps bumping its tusk into the side of a large Construction (工) beam, always pushing it to the opposite side from where it needs to go.
左.onyomi: The sah-ndals were left on the wrong foot, making it impossible to walk straight.
左.kunyomi: Hidari — 'he'd hurry' — he'd hurry if he knew he was supposed to turn left back there.

本.meaning: The Book (本) itself is the fundamental source of all knowledge, its pages containing the very origin of stories.
本.onyomi: Hans consults his instruction book, making sure every step is followed precisely.
本.kunyomi: Moto — 'moh-toh' — the moto-cycle's engine is the very origin of its power.

白.meaning: The White (白) radical itself is a pristine canvas, reflecting pure, untainted light.
白.onyomi: The hack-er's screen went completely white, erasing all his data.
白.kunyomi: Shiro — 'she-row' — a pure white rowboat glides silently across the lake.

万.meaning: A single Leaf falls, but as it touches the ground, a mischievous Sword (刀) slices it into so many tiny fragments that there are ten thousand pieces.
万.onyomi: A man stood bewildered, facing ten thousand choices for his next meal.
万.kunyomi: Yorozu — 'your roo-zoo' — your zoo needs ten thousand more animals to be complete.

今.meaning: The very shape of the Now (今) radical captures the fleeting moment, present and immediate.
今.onyomi: Kin carefully polishes a tiny gold charm, knowing that its value is highest right now.
今.kunyomi: Ima — 'ee-mah' — 'E-mail me now!' she shouted, needing the information immediately.

午.meaning: The sun begins to Slide down from its peak, making the air feel Dry (干) as it approaches the middle of the day.
午.onyomi: Go! It's already noon, we need to leave!
午.kunyomi: Uma — 'ooh-mah' — 'Ooh, ma!' she exclaimed, realizing it was noon and she'd missed lunch.

友.meaning: A Narwhal gently nudges a Stool towards you, inviting you to sit and share a secret, a true sign of a good relationship.
友.onyomi: Yusuf always has a kind word for his friends, offering them comfort and support.
友.kunyomi: Tomo — 'toe-moh' — a friend will always help you if you stub your toe on a moh-mentous occasion.

父.meaning: The powerful stance of the Father (父) radical evokes a protective figure, a patriarch.
父.onyomi: Fuad, the merchant, always sought his father's advice on important business deals.
父.kunyomi: Chichi — 'chee-chee' — 'Chee-chee!' cried the baby, reaching for his father.

北.meaning: Two Fingers, stiff with cold, try to hold a Spoon, shivering uncontrollably because they've ventured too far North.
北.onyomi: The Hulk, shivering in the cold, points towards the North.
北.kunyomi: A kitten shivers, pointing its nose towards the North wind.

半.meaning: A massive Triceratops is so parched that it's become completely Dry (干), withered away until only Half of its body remains.
半.onyomi: Hans meticulously measures a cake, making sure to cut it exactly in Half.
半.kunyomi: You only have Half a nacho left, how sad!

外.meaning: As Evening (夕) falls, you stub your Toe on the doorstep, realizing you're still standing Outside.
外.onyomi: Kai, having been at sea too long, yearns to step Outside onto solid land.
外.kunyomi: You leave your comfy sofa and step Outside into the cold.

母.meaning: A Mother stands under the relentless Sun (日), a single Drop (落) of sweat, or perhaps a tear, rolling down her face as she cares for her children.
母.onyomi: Bo, despite his tough exterior, always calls his Mother every Sunday.
母.kunyomi: Your Mother laughs, "Ha-ha!", when you tell her a funny story.

休.meaning: The weary Leader (長) finally finds a moment of peace, leaning against a sturdy Tree (木) to take a well-deserved Rest.
休.onyomi: Kyu, exhausted from rushing, finally gets a chance to Rest.
休.kunyomi: You lean back on your yacht and Rest.

先.meaning: With a powerful push of his Legs, the runner takes a running Slide in the Dirt, crossing the finish line just Before his opponent.
先.onyomi: Senna always aims to be Before everyone else at the start of the race.
先.kunyomi: You finish your sake just Before your friend.

名.meaning: In the quiet of the Evening (夕), a mother calls out her child's Name with her Mouth (口) to come home.
名.onyomi: "May I know your Name?" you ask politely.
名.kunyomi: "Nah, I don't know her Name," you reply.

年.meaning: Every Year, the Cow (牛) has to run from the hunter's Gun (弓).
年.onyomi: The neon sign lights up, celebrating the New Year.
年.kunyomi: We raise a toast to the New Year.

気.meaning: A hidden Treasure (宝) chest, when opened, releases a surge of pure Energy (力) – the very Spirit of adventure.
気.onyomi: Kiki's bubbly Spirit fills the room with laughter.
気.kunyomi: The ancient ink holds the Spirit of the old master.

百.meaning: A single Leaf falls from the tree, but under the bright Sun (日), you can see there are a Hundred more still clinging on.
百.onyomi: You count a Hundred yaks grazing under the sun.
百.kunyomi: You eat a Hundred momo dumplings, feeling full.

男.meaning: A strong figure stands tall in the Rice Paddy (田), putting all their Power (力) into working the land, fulfilling a traditional role.
男.onyomi: Dan, with his broad shoulders, is a powerful male who can lift anything.
男.kunyomi: Oh, a toe caught in the Rice Paddy (田)! Only a strong male would laugh it off.

見.meaning: An eye on legs stands tall, always ready to See (見) everything around it, observing the world.
見.onyomi: Kenny squints, trying to See (見) the tiny leak in the pipe.
見.kunyomi: Me? I can See (見) everything from this vantage point!

車.meaning: The four sturdy wheels and chassis of the Car (車) are ready to roll down any road, carrying passengers far and wide.
車.onyomi: Sheila jumps into her rugged Car (車), ready to herd sheep across the vast land.
車.kunyomi: The whole crew piled into the Car (車) for an epic road trip.

毎.meaning: Every morning, the same ritual: a Gun (弓) is meticulously cleaned and placed by the Window (窓), ready for the day.
毎.onyomi: My routine is the same Every single day, without fail.
毎.kunyomi: Go to the window Every morning and watch the sunrise.

行.meaning: A long, winding path stretches out, inviting you to Go (行) forward, one step at a time.
行.onyomi: Kofi is always Going (行) somewhere new to find wood for his projects.
行.kunyomi: Eve is Going (行) to explore the new botanical garden.

西.meaning: The Sun dips below the horizon in the West (西), painting the sky with fiery, fading colors.
西.onyomi: Selma stubbornly insisted on building her house facing the West (西).
西.kunyomi: The sun sets beautifully in that niche of the West (西) sky.

何.meaning: The Leader (長) points a stern finger at the strange Lip Ring, demanding, 'What (何) is that thing?'
何.onyomi: Carlos rapidly asks, 'What (何) do you need? What (何) can I sell you?'
何.kunyomi: The nanny asked, 'What (何) did you do to your room?'

来.meaning: The villagers eagerly watch the fertile Ground (地), waiting for the first tender shoots of Rice (米) to Come (来) forth.
来.onyomi: Tai, the massive rugby player, will Come (来) to our village for the festival.
来.kunyomi: Kyu always manages to Come (来) late to class.

学.meaning: A mighty Viking, surprisingly patient, sits with a curious Child (子), helping them Study (学) the ancient runic script.
学.onyomi: A 'gag' order was placed on the Viking so he would Study (学) quietly with the Child (子).
学.kunyomi: The child received manna from heaven to help him Study (学) his lessons.

金.meaning: A shimmering nugget of Gold (金) is unearthed from the depths of the earth, glinting with precious value.
金.onyomi: Kin, the meticulous goldsmith, polishes a new piece of Gold (金) jewelry.
金.kunyomi: The old man's cane was tipped with pure Gold (金).

雨.meaning: The symbol for Rain (雨) itself perfectly depicts drops falling from the sky, washing over everything, bringing the very essence of a downpour.
雨.onyomi: You can hear the rain pattering outside, a soft 'U' sound against the window.
雨.kunyomi: A may shower brings gentle rain to the garden, nurturing new growth.

国.meaning: A King (王) stands within the vast Mouth (口) of his borders, feeling a tiny Drop (落) of responsibility for the entire realm under his rule.
国.onyomi: The cook traveled to many different countries to learn their unique cuisines.
国.kunyomi: You get on your knee to propose in your home country, a place of personal significance.

東.meaning: The Sun (日) rises, its first golden rays peeking over the top of a tall Tree (木) in the distance, marking the direction of the dawn.
東.onyomi: Tova wakes at 4 am, always facing east to greet the rising sun and start her day.
東.kunyomi: He got she (a map) to find her way to the east, where the adventure begins.

長.meaning: The radical Long (長) itself depicts a person with a long, flowing beard and a staff, symbolizing extended length and seniority.
長.onyomi: Cho's noodle dishes are always incredibly long, stretching across the table as she serves them.
長.kunyomi: The naga snake is incredibly long, its body winding through the ancient forest.

前.meaning: Under the serene light of the Moon (月), a creature with prominent Horns kneels on the Ground (地), presenting an offering directly in front of an ancient altar.
前.onyomi: Achieving a Zen state helps you focus on what's right in front of you, clearing your mind.
前.kunyomi: My car is parked right in front of the house, exactly where I left it.

南.meaning: A wild beast with sharp Horns lowers its Head (首) and charges, its path forming a perfect Cross (十) shape, always heading towards the warm winds from the south.
南.onyomi: My Nan always goes south for the winter to escape the cold, following the migratory birds.
南.kunyomi: Many mommy birds fly south for the winter, seeking warmer climates for their chicks.

後.meaning: In the harsh Winter (冬) snow, a person is forced to Loiter behind, because they stepped in Poop and need to clean their shoes before entering.
後.onyomi: Go, but don't forget to look behind you for danger, always be aware of your surroundings.
後.kunyomi: No cheat will get ahead; the true winner will come from behind, earning their victory.

食.meaning: The radical Eat (食) itself clearly shows a mouth with food inside, ready to be consumed and nourish the body.
食.onyomi: It's a shock how much food Sho can eat after a day of surfing, he's always hungry.
食.kunyomi: The baby coos happily after it eats, its hunger satisfied and belly full.

校.meaning: Under the watchful eye of the Father (父), a student sits beneath a Tree (木), a heavy Lid covering their exam paper until the start signal is given.
校.onyomi: Kofi studied hard for his exam, hoping to pass and achieve his academic goals.

時.meaning: The Sun (日) moves across the sky, casting shadows on the Temple (寺) steps — monks track time by watching where the light falls.
時.onyomi: Ji carefully inks the time onto his calligraphy scrolls, each stroke a moment preserved.
時.kunyomi: You stub your toe on the temple keystone every time you're late, a painful reminder of the passing time.

高.meaning: A person with a prominent Mustache stands on a giant Mouth (口) and then stacks a Lid on top of their head, attempting to appear as... tall as possible.
高.onyomi: Kofi, the carpenter, stands on a ladder so tall he can reach the highest beams.
高.kunyomi: You need a tall stack of tacos to satisfy your hunger after a long day.

間.meaning: The Sun (日) slowly crosses the sky, its rays shining through the opening of a grand Gate (門), marking the passage of each day's interval.
間.onyomi: Khan, the warlord, commands his army to march in precise intervals between battles.
間.kunyomi: There's an interval of silence between the 'ah' of surprise and the 'mah' of disbelief.

話.meaning: To Say (言) a compelling Tale, one must use their Tongue (舌) to weave words carefully, making sure every syllable lands just right.
話.onyomi: The old storyteller would make a 'wah' sound to emphasize the dramatic parts of his tale.
話.kunyomi: Hanna loved to tell a long and winding tale to anyone who would listen.

電.meaning: During a fierce Rain (雨) storm, an Umbrella (傘) stands upright in a flooded Rice Paddy (田), acting as a lightning rod, drawing a powerful spark of electricity.
電.onyomi: The mad scientist's den was crackling with strange electricity and experiments.

聞.meaning: An enormous Ear (耳) presses against the heavy Gate (門), straining to Hear every whisper from beyond the wall.
聞.onyomi: You can hear the crunch of the fresh bun as you bite into it, a delicious sound.
聞.kunyomi: The sound of a key turning in the lock makes you strain to hear who's coming.

語.meaning: With a Mouth (口) wide open, you Say (言) exactly Five (五) distinct words, each one carefully chosen and enunciated.
語.onyomi: With a single word, 'Go!', the race began.
語.kunyomi: A good storyteller knows how to cater their words to their audience.

読.meaning: To Say (言) the sales pitch well, you must carefully Read the contract you plan to Sell (売), making sure you understand every clause.
読.onyomi: The old sailor loved to read a good book down by the dock.
読.kunyomi: You read the note, which simply said, 'Yo, what's up?'

生.meaning: The radical 'Life (生)' itself, a vibrant green sprout, pushes through the earth, a testament to its enduring power and resilience.
生.onyomi: Sho, the surfer, lives a laid-back life on the beach, always chasing the next wave.
生.kunyomi: Eve, the botanist, dedicated her life to studying the mysteries of plants.

書.meaning: As the Sun (日) rises, illuminating the ancient scrolls, a scholar takes up their Brush (掃) to meticulously Write down the day's observations.
書.onyomi: Sho, the surfer, likes to write poetry about the ocean and the endless horizon.
書.kunyomi: Carlos, the street vendor, quickly writes down customer orders, never missing a beat.
